section.content: Embodiments of the present disclosure relate to artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model Identifier (ID) use. A terminal device sends a request for AI/ML model registration or identification to a core network device, wherein the request includes at least one AI/ML model capability of the terminal device. The terminal device receives a response to the AI/ML model registration or identification from the core network device, wherein the response includes approving or identifying the AI/ML model ID list and at least one AI/ML model delivery preference. The solution provided in the present disclosure for AI/ML model identifier ID usage may provide a signaling procedure that needs to be defined between the terminal device and the network to determine the validity of a given AI/ML model and allow the network to further query the terminal device for capabilities related to AI/ML model(s).

Technical Field

Various example embodiments relate generally to the field of communications and, in particular, relate to devices, methods, apparatuses, and computer-readable storage media for artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model Identifier (ID) use.

Background

With the development of communication technology, an AI/ML model for a New Radio (NR) air interface has been studied. In third generation partnership project (3 GPP) release 18 (Rel-18) Study Item (SI), the benefits of enhancing the air interface with features enabling support for AI/ML based algorithms have been explored to improve performance and/or reduce complexity and overhead.

The initial set of use cases to be covered in Rel-18 SI includes CSI feedback enhancements (e.g., overhead reduction, accuracy improvement, prediction), beam management (e.g., time and/or spatial beam prediction for overhead and delay reduction, beam selection accuracy improvement), and positioning accuracy enhancement. The use cases of the AI/ML approach need to be sufficiently diverse to support the various requirements of the next generation node B (gNB) -User Equipment (UE) cooperation level, which define at least the combination of ML models applied at the UE and/or gNB.

The goal of Rel-18 SI is to lay a foundation for future air interface use cases that utilize AI/ML technology. For AI/ML use cases, its advantages (with developed methods and defined KPIs) should be evaluated, and potential impact on the specification, including PHY layer aspects and protocol aspects, should be evaluated. One of the expected results of SI is that "AI/ML approach to selected sub-use cases needs to be sufficiently diverse to support the various requirements of the gNB-UE cooperation level. "

It should be noted that other use cases may also be involved in the Work Item (WI) phase of AI/ML for air interface. Starting from Rel-18, a number of use cases and applications for AI/ML are proposed in the gNB and UE. The goal is to explore the benefits of enabling enhanced support for AI/ML-based algorithms to improve performance and/or reduce complexity/overhead by enhancing features of the air interface. The enhanced performance here depends on the use case considered and may, for example, improve throughput, robustness, accuracy, reliability, etc. The goal is to consider enough use cases to enable the identification of generic AI/ML frameworks, including the functional requirements of the AI/ML framework, which can be used for subsequent projects. The study should also identify areas where AI/ML can improve the performance of air interface functions. The specification impact will be evaluated to improve the overall understanding of what is needed to enable AI/ML technology for the air interface.

According to the discussion in RAN1/RAN2, UEs supporting ML models to enhance a given function in the specification (e.g., beam management, CSI reporting) will use AI/ML model IDs (which may also be referred to as ML model IDs) to identify ML models (e.g., CSI compression, CSI prediction, time domain beam prediction, spatial domain beam prediction, ML-based positioning are all underlying functions) corresponding to the function being used. However, it is not clear how the network should know/identify which specific AI/ML model IDs are valid. Validity here may represent a number of things, such as that the underlying ML model has been validated, can be used by the UE, tested, verified, authenticated, authorized for use, can be configured for the UE, and so forth. This is even more important because the network cannot understand what is behind the ML model (typically this is a deep neural network and it cannot be expected that the network will understand architectural and implementation aspects, because this is typically a choice of machine learning implementation, and there are typically hundreds of different options and variants to choose from, and details are typically proprietary and not public).

It is not clear how, after the network can reliably determine the "valid" AI/ML model IDs, the capabilities corresponding to these IDs can be retrieved from the UE so that the UE can be configured to take these into account. Furthermore, there is no answer how the network can transfer the ML model architecture representation (which can be encoded in OCETS sets using well known tools, see for example ONNX format) to the UE.

It is contemplated that a signaling procedure needs to be defined between the UE and the network to determine the validity of a given ML model and to allow the network to further query the UE for capabilities related to these ML model(s). Solving the above problems requires the following aspects:

The present application defines a new procedure for 1) ML model storage in newly defined network logical nodes, 2) verification and activation of AI/ML model ID(s) at UE and gNB, 3) UE capability model query and configuration (which may also be implemented via model function query and configuration).

Accordingly, the present disclosure proposes an AI/ML model identification and capability handling for UE(s). Referring to fig. 1A, an example network environment 100A is illustrated in which example embodiments of the present disclosure may be implemented.
